label: Telegram
terms_note: Free, no review: create a bot with @BotFather and use its token; the bot must be an ADMINISTRATOR of a channel to post there; bots cannot message a user who has not started them; bots in groups see only commands / replies unless privacy mode is off; limits ≈ 30 messages/s overall, 20 messages/min per group, 1 message/s per chat (429 with retry_after); user-account automation (MTProto) is a different product and is off-limits for the suite (human lane).

sdks: python-telegram-bot / aiogram / telegraf (community; Telegram lists them)

tools.name: read_comments
tools.endpoint: getUpdates (long polling) / setWebhook — channel discussion replies arrive as updates

tools.name: analytics_post
tools.endpoint: — (no per-message analytics for bots; channel view counts are not exposed to the Bot API)

auth: 1. The tenant creates a bot with **@BotFather** → token (stored encrypted as the account secret).
2. Add the bot as **administrator** of the channel (post messages right) or to the group.
3. Updates: `setWebhook` (HTTPS URL, `secret_token` header check) OR `getUpdates` long polling — mutually exclusive.
4. No review, no fee. Bots cannot initiate chats with users who never messaged them.

endpoints.call: sendMessage` {chat_id (@channelusername or id), text ≤ 4096, parse_mode HTML

endpoints.purpose: multipart upload ≤ 50 MB via API, or URL / file_id

endpoints.call: sendMessage` with `reply_parameters{message_id}`; in discussion groups reply to the forwarded post
webhook `Update` objects: message, channel_post, edited_channel_post, callback_query, message_reaction
endpoints.purpose: privacy mode hides non-command group messages unless disabled

endpoints.call: getChatMemberCount`, `getChat`; channel post `views` only through MTProto — no Bot API analytics

reference.limits: - ~30 messages/s overall, 20 messages/min into one group, 1 message/s per chat; HTTP 429 with `parameters.retry_after`. - Bot API Terms of Service: no spam / unsolicited messages; a bot's content is the operator's responsibility. - Automating **user** accounts (MTProto) is out of scope — human lane per the Messaging rules.

fields.name: token
fields.help: Bot token from @BotFather. It is part of the URL path: 'All queries to the Telegram Bot API must be served over HTTPS and need to be presented in this form: https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/METHOD_NAME' (https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#making-requests). The bot must be an administrator of the target channel with the right to post (and delete) messages. Same field as the messaging entry (env PLATFORM_MCP_TELEGRAM_TOKEN).

config_fields.name: chat_id
config_fields.help: The channel (or group) the bot publishes to, sent as `chat_id`: 'Unique identifier for the target chat or username of the target channel (in the format @channelusername)', e.g. @mychannel or -1001234567890; env PLATFORM_MCP_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID. Message ids are unique only inside this chat, so `post_id` values are message_ids of this chat.

adapter.envelope_note: Every response is 'a JSON object, which always has a Boolean field ok' with `description`, `error_code` and `parameters` (retry_after) on failure (https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#making-requests). ok:false answers become isError results.
adapter.rate_note: Bot FAQ: 'avoid sending more than one message per second' in a chat, 'not more than 20 messages per minute' in a group, 'about 30 messages per second' overall; 429 with retry_after (https://core.telegram.org/bots/faq). One client-side bucket at 1/s.

me.note: getMe: 'A simple method for testing your bot's authentication token. Requires no parameters. Returns basic information about the bot in form of a User object' (id, is_bot, first_name, username).

publish_text.note: sendMessage {chat_id: <configured chat_id>, text ('Text of the message to be sent, 1-4096 characters after entities parsing'), reply_parameters?} - 'On success, the sent Message is returned'; `id` is the Message's message_id ('Unique message identifier inside this chat'), so it identifies the post only together with the configured chat. `reply_to` (a message_id in the same chat) is sent as reply_parameters.message_id ('Identifier of the message that will be replied to in the current chat, or in the chat chat_id if it is specified'; the Bot API server parses integer fields from JSON strings as well as numbers, tdlib JsonBuilder get_integer_field). parse_mode is not sent (plain text); no url, and `date` is a Unix timestamp under raw.date, so created_at is not mapped.

delete.note: deleteMessage {chat_id: <configured chat_id>, message_id: post_id ('Identifier of the message to delete')} 'Returns True on success' (the runtime answers {status: 'deleted'}; a failure is an ok:false envelope error). Limitations: 'A message can only be deleted if it was sent less than 48 hours ago', 'Bots granted can_post_messages permissions can delete outgoing messages in channels', 'If the bot is an administrator of a group, it can delete any message there', 'If the bot has can_delete_messages administrator right in a supergroup or a channel, it can delete any message there'. A message outside the configured chat cannot be addressed.

publish_image.note: sendPhoto {chat_id: <configured chat_id>, photo: image_urls[0] ('pass an HTTP URL as a String for Telegram to get a photo from the Internet ... The photo must be at most 10 MB in size'), caption: text ('Photo caption ..., 0-1024 characters after entities parsing')} - 'On success, the sent Message is returned'; `id` is the message_id inside the configured chat. Only the FIRST image URL is sent (sendMediaGroup, the 2-10 item album method, is not used); further image_urls are ignored. parse_mode is not sent; no url / created_at (raw.date is a Unix timestamp).

not_offered.read_comments: The Bot API has no method that returns the messages or replies of a chat: comments on channel posts live in the linked discussion group and reach the bot only as updates through getUpdates or a webhook (https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#getting-updates).
not_offered.reply_comment: A comment is a message in the channel's linked discussion group, a different chat from the configured chat_id; the bot cannot list comments (no read method) and sendMessage with reply_parameters needs that group's chat_id, which the vocabulary does not carry (https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendmessage).
not_offered.read_mentions: No mention feed: mentions arrive only as `mention` / `text_mention` entities on incoming messages delivered through getUpdates or a webhook, and bots in groups see other messages only when privacy mode is off (https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#getting-updates).
not_offered.analytics_post: The Bot API documents no per-message statistics method and its Message object carries no view or reaction counters; the only counter available to bots is getChatMemberCount for the whole chat (https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#available-methods).
